query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to produce the improvement, a measurable outcome relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with clear observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Intervention of alloying elements can improve hardness and strength in high-entropy alloys without sacrificing mechanical performance
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of solid solutions and precipitation of strengthening phases
generation.mechanism: Enhanced lattice distortion and precipitation hardening
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy alloys with specific compositions and processing conditions
generation.uncertainty: Further research is needed to fully understand the effects of alloying elements on mechanical performance
generation.falsification_experiment: Comparison of mechanical properties between alloyed and unalloyed high-entropy alloys under controlled conditions
